subject: DataForge — networking capacity & streaming readiness (post-demo)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Abby Li <abby@dataforge.com>, Net Team <net-team@dataforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: DataForge — networking capacity & streaming readiness (post-demo)

Hi Abby / Net Team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate you walking through the inference flow and the sample traffic profile. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the Private deployment preflight and SLO validation: 

Recap / asks from our side:
- Target SLOs we discussed: median request latency ~<200ms (streaming median), 95th percentile ≤700ms, tail (99th) budget ≤1s for worst-case flows. Please confirm those numbers are still accurate.
- Concurrency profile: you mentioned steady-state ~120 concurrent sessions, peak burst up to ~350 concurrent streams. We need expected sustained qps and average token-per-request if available so we can size KV cache and batching.
- Throughput / egress: observed per-stream outbound bandwidth ~200-400 kbps; recommend we baseline for 500 kbps per stream to be conservative.
- Networking topology: we need the VPC CIDRs, whether you plan VPN tunnel(s) or direct peering (AWS Direct Connect / GCP Interconnect), and whether NAT gateway/bastion paths will be in the traffic flow.
- Test window: propose a 2-hour preflight test where we replay representative streaming traffic (ramp to peak, hold, and burst). We will run packet captures and application-level traces.

Attachments: demo recording, a short acceptance checklist (Redwood), and please attach the network diagram if you can.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share the network diagram and a contact for Net Team who can approve peering/VPN config (reply with e-mail + preferred times).
2) We align on exact SLO numbers and the concurrency/avg request-size numbers by EOD Wed 8/11.
3) Redwood provides a preflight test plan (we'll include wireguard/keystone steps for the private plane) and a proposed test window for week of 8/16.

Ben / Monica — can you weigh in on the test harness and a succinct runbook we can share with DataForge? I propose we include packet captures + per-request latency histograms at 50ms bins and an egress bandwidth tracker.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (video), redwood-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Abby Li <abby@dataforge.com>

Cc: Net Team <net-team@dataforge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 17:30:15 -0700
Subject: Re: DataForge — networking capacity & streaming readiness (post-demo)

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- SLO confirmation: our product team is asking for median <250ms and 95th <750ms for streaming sessions. The numbers you suggested look conservative and acceptable; well try to tighten them internally but please plan for the slightly higher 95th for initial acceptance.
- Concurrency: steady-state ~120 concurrent sessions is correct; peak simultaneous streams historically up to 350 (short bursts, ~5-10 minutes). Average request size (tokens) varies by integration: minimal chat flows ~40 tokens, longer sessions ~300 tokens.
- Egress: typical per-stream egress ~300 kbps but can spike to ~600 kbps on media-heavy sessions; we can provide a weekly pcap sample and the network diagram (attach).

We'll attach the network diagram and loop in our infra lead (net-team) for peering details. Our preference is to start with an encrypted VPN tunnel first, then evaluate direct peering once the baseline is validated.

Available times for a short topology handoff call: Tue 8/10 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 8/11 14:00-15:00 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks,
Abby Li
Senior Platform PM, DataForge
abby@dataforge.com

Attachments: df-network-diagram.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:11:30 -0700
Subject: RE: DataForge — networking capacity & streaming readiness (post-demo)

Karthik / team,

Good notes. A few internal points before we lock a slot with DataForge: 

1) Test harness: I recommend we run the following in the preflight:
   - Ramp test: 0 -> 120 concurrent streams over 10 mins, hold 30 mins.
   - Burst test: 120 -> 350 over 5 mins, hold 10 mins, then drop.
   - Long-tail test: 1 hour at 120 with periodic 30s high-bandwidth spikes to simulate media.
   - Metrics: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), token throughput, per-stream egress.

2) Connectivity options: VPN first, then peering. For VPN we need the Net Team to confirm MTU and IPsec rekey timings — those have caused tail latency spikes in past on-prem engagements. If they plan NAT in the path, we should ask for source-preserving NAT or an alternate SNAT pool.

3) Observability hooks: we will need a temporary debug role for our traceroute/pcap collection (time-limited), plus a shared S3 bucket or Drive link to drop captures. Monica, can you draft a scoped access policy we can send to DataForge?

4) Acceptance gates: propose these minimal pass criteria for initial sign-off: p50 < 300ms, p95 < 800ms, no packet loss >0.5% sustained. We can tighten these after canary.

Ill assemble a short one-page test plan and runbook and share by EOD.

-Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

- Preflight tests: Redwood proposes Tue 8/17 09:00-11:00 PT for the first window. During the window we will perform the ramp, burst, and long-tail tests described below.
- Connectivity: Ok to start with VPN tunnel. Net Team, please confirm MTU, whether there is NAT in the path, and an IR contact for the test window.
